hook_text: Your tower sketch is about to become something a builder can cut from. Three views, one sheet, every number real.
clip_script: A working drawing is instructions. Three flat views, lined up, first-angle: front in the middle showing the A and the back-leg's slope; plan below showing the base and where the leg's foot lands; side view on the right showing the width and the bracing. Scale 1 to 5 on A3, written in the title block, but every number is full size: 600 means cut 600. Lines mean things: thick for what you see, dashed for hidden, chain for centres. Dimension once, where clearest; the back-leg by its two ends, never its slope; bracing nodes as a chain up the leg. Now the winder, drawn where it lives: drum and motor as rectangles, gears as circles in the side view with centre distances from your gear sheet, rope from drum to sheave to cage, brake where it bites. Number every part, list them with lengths and quantities. That list is next week's budget and build order.
visual_style: A3 sheet divides into three aligned views; an A-frame appears with thick, dashed and chain lines colour-coded; dimension chains climb a leg; drum, gears and rope slot into place; balloon numbers fly to a parts list.
pacing: Three views, scale, lines, dimensions, the winder in place, the parts list.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and lay out the three view boxes for your headgear on a sheet tonight.
